title: Guiding Diffusion Language Models with Denoising Entropy
claim: Uncertainty accumulated along a generation path predicts output quality: paths with lower aggregate uncertainty yield better final outputs.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line; left definitions, right three branching decoding paths
description: The figure has two panels separated by a vertical dashed line. The left panel shows a 3x3 number-grid puzzle, called a State, with some cells masked. Beside it is a stack of grids, called a Path. A red arrow links the two, and a red ellipse highlights the masked cells. Below is a pink legend box that defines three uncertainty levels. H is the uncertainty at a position, h_DE is the uncertainty of a state, and H_DE is the uncertainty of a path. The right panel starts from one partially filled grid and a green 'Decoding Strategy' box. Three arrows branch from it into three decoding trajectories. Each trajectory has a gauge dial labeled h_DE and ends in a completed grid. The top path is green and ends in a checkmark with H_DE 0.9. The middle and bottom paths are red and pink and end in red X marks with 1.5 and 1.6. A long red 'Decoding' arrow runs along the bottom.
caption: Quantifying Path Uncertainty in MDMs with Denoising Entropy. Left: State Entropy ($\entropyState$) measures per-state uncertainty, computed as the mean Shannon Entropy over the predictive distributions for all masked positions. $\entropyState$ is then aggregated over the entire path to form the Path Entropy ($\entropyPath$). Right: Decoding process shows how different paths yield outputs of varying quality. Our key insight is that the lower $\entropyPath$ indicates path yeilding better output, providing a potent internal signal for generation quality.
abstract: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) offer flexible, non-autoregressive generation, but this freedom introduces a challenge: final output quality is highly sensitive to the decoding order. We are the first to formalize this issue, attributing the variability in output quality to the cumulative predictive uncertainty along a generative path. To quantify this uncertainty, we introduce Denoising Entropy, a computable metric that serves as an internal signal for evaluating generative process. Leveraging this metric, we propose two algorithms designed to optimize the decoding path: a post-hoc selection method and a real-time guidance strategy. Experiments demonstrate that our entropy-guided methods significantly improve generation quality, consistently boosting accuracy on challenging reasoning, planning, and code benchmarks. Our work establishes Denoising Entropy as a principled tool for understanding and controlling generation, effectively turning the uncertainty in DLMs from a liability into a key advantage for discovering high-quality solutions.
